name: flatpak
description: A cross-distribution application framework: desktop apps ship with their own runtimes and sandboxed permissions, independent of the system package manager.

flags.description: Add a repository (Flathub is the main one).
Update all installed apps and runtimes.

examples.explanation: One-time setup: adds Flathub, the main application store.
Installs GIMP sandboxed, bundled with its own runtime libraries.
Updates all Flatpak apps and runtimes independently of the system package manager.

Name      Application ID        Version
GIMP      org.gimp.GIMP         2.10.38
examples.explanation: Shows installed applications with their IDs.

about: Flatpak apps run in sandboxes with explicit permissions (filesystem, devices, IPC) managed via overrides: flatpak override --filesystem=home org.app. They are ideal for getting current desktop software on stable/enterprise distributions. Snap (Canonical) and AppImage are the comparable cross-distro formats.
useCases: Install fresh desktop apps on Debian stable, RHEL, or any distro.
mistakes: Expecting Flatpak apps in CLI pipelines — it targets desktop apps; runtimes make installs large.
Forgetting to add the Flathub remote first.
distroNotes: Works on nearly all distributions; preinstalled on Fedora. Debian/Ubuntu install it via apt first.
